newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cricket-Vettori joins NZ spin merry-go-round.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Vettori joins NZ spin merry-go-round.

text.p: Daniel Vettori's shock inclusion in the New Zealand 12 for this week's second cricket test against England continues the selectors search for a longterm international class spinner.

Since the second half of the 1980s, when left arm spinner Stephen Boock and offspinner John Bracewell held sway in New Zealand teams, it has become a merry-go-round for candidates as the national selectors spread their search around the country.
Bracewell went to England in 1990 on his last tour, and had left armer Mark Priest for spin bowling company.
Priest went to Pakistan later that year along with two offspinners, Grant Bradburn and Dipak Patel.
When New Zealand toured Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka in 1992, Patel was joined by another left armer Mark Haslam, then just 20.

By the time of the England tour of 1994, Matthew Hart had supplanted Haslam as the preferred left arm spinner, having helped New Zealand to a test win over Pakistan at Christchurch early that year, when he was 21.
Hart took eight wickets as New Zealand beat South Africa at Johannesburg late in 1994 and 15 wickets in the three-test series seemed to suggest he was there for the long stretch.
Instead he has played only five more tests, taking just three wickets.

Legspinner Greg Loveridge was called in, aged 20, for his test debut against Zimbabwe in January, 1996, but fractured a finger before he could bowl and with other injuries having dogged his progress is still trying to make his way back into the frame.
Along the way, Haslam returned briefly for two tests and Patel has kept his place, in between injuries and the occasional selection whim.
So Vettori, who turned 18 on January 27 and has played only two first-class matches, both last month, is the latest to get a chance to establish himself in the New Zealand test team.
He's already taken one significant step, according to chairman of selectors Ross Dykes.
"He's developed so quickly that he's at the head of our left arm slow bowlers," he said.
"I just think every now and then you get somebody special, and if the head is right age is only a number."
